title: From Chatbots to Confidants: A Cross-Cultural Study of LLM Adoption for Emotional Support
measurement_description: The paper evaluated how a user's demographic background, specifically their religious affiliation and belief status (believers vs. non-believers), influences their adoption rates, trust, perceived benefits, and usage intention regarding Large Language Models for emotional support.
findings: The study found that religious individuals (believers) report significantly more positive perceptions of LLMs for emotional support—including higher trust, perceived benefits, and usage intention—compared to non-believers. The differences between specific religions (e.g., Christianity vs. Islam) were insignificant compared to the broader divide between believers and non-believers.
